title: Regulatory residency review with Aurora Financial - data & compliance
summary: Discovery focused on data residency, GDPR/HIPAA applicability, and log retention constraints for Aurora Financial's LLM use-cases. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary concern is legal/regulatory auditability, ability to restrict logs, and encryption/KMS control. Redwood AE/SE clarified deployment options, SOC2/ISO posture, KMS integrations, and proposed a Private deployment pilot with limited hosted fallback. Agreed next steps: share security whitepaper, SOC2 report, and configure pilot SOW and PoC checklist.
topics: GDPR data subject requests & right to be forgotten
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Audit evidence and SOC2 / ISO attestations
action_items: Alex Morris; Share SOC2 + ISO attestation PDFs and security whitepaper; 2025-03-14
Priya Shah; Provide proposed architecture diagram for Private deployment with KMS flow; 2025-03-18
Jason Park; Provide sample dataset description & list of PHI fields we expect to send; 2025-03-17
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, penetration test summary)
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) with Platform and CISO for week of 3/24
Draft pilot statement of work for Private deployment and limited hosted fallback
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morris (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions Eng), Daniel Reed (Aurora CISO), Maria Lopez (Aurora Head of Cloud), Sophie Tan (Aurora Legal), Jason Park (Aurora Platform)

Auto-summary: brief discussion on residency and compliance, clarified Redwood deployment options and logging behaviors, agreed to exchange docs and schedule pilot SOW review.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood Inference, I'll kick off, we got Priya and Liam from the solution team here. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Daniel Reed: Good, thanks. We wanted to make sure we cover the heavy compliance stuff up front — residency, logs, HIPAA implications.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Absolutely, that's what we're here for. Just to set expectations, we'll talk through Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options and how each aligns with regulatory controls.
[00:25] Maria Lopez: Quick context — Aurora's planning to surface LLM-driven assistants across customer support and loan underwriting pipelines. Some payloads might include PII and in a few flows, potentially PHI tied to insurance products. So us ensuring data never leaves EU/UK datacenters for EU customers is critical.
[00:42] Alex Morris: Understood. Can you confirm the scope — is the ask regional storage only, or also processing locality?
[00:48] Jason Park: Processing has to be regional for EU subjects, so both storage and compute should be in-region. We've had auditors push back on any cross-border processing without explicit legal basis.
[00:58] Sophie Tan: Also, we need support for DSARs — right to be forgotten. We need a clear deletion path and proof for auditors.
[01:07] Priya Shah: For deletion, we support per-customer data deletion on Private and Dedicated; Hosted is more nuanced because of shared infra and backups — we can provide retention and purge controls but full guarantees are easier with Private where you control storage.
[01:22] Daniel Reed: That makes sense. What about logging? Our security policy says minimal logging of content and strict retention. We can't allow full transcripts to sit in logs for 90 days.
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: Right. On Redwood's side we have configurable logging levels. For Private and Dedicated we can disable content-level logs and only retain metadata tokens and request IDs. On Hosted, we can limit but there are product telemetry requirements; we discussed options like stripping prompt/response from logs before writing to telemetry.
[01:50] Maria Lopez: Is there an option for suppressing prompt text in any logs at all?
[01:54] Priya Shah: Yes, with Private deployment you can route logs to your customers' logging endpoints only — you can ingest or drop content. With Dedicated we offer log redaction rules, and we can do field-level redaction: mask or hash certain fields before persisting.
[02:08] Sophie Tan: How do you prove to an auditor that redaction actually happened? We need evidence for audit trails.
[02:14] Alex Morris: Good Q. We provide audit logs for configuration changes and can provide scrubbed request logs with hashes that map to user requests. For higher assurance, Private deployment gives you full control over where logs are stored and you can retain the raw logs in your own vault if needed.
[02:31] Daniel Reed: KMS — we need customer-controlled keys, ideally HSM-backed, and want to ensure Redwood never has access to plaintext keys.
[02:40] Priya Shah: We support external KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can use customer-managed keys in supported cloud providers but there's a trust boundary — for the highest assurance we recommend Private with an HSM or customer-owned KMS and key wrapping.
[02:55] Jason Park: Does that cover model weights and cache? For example, are KV caches stored encrypted under the same KMS?
[03:01] Liam O'Connor: The KV cache and intermediate state can be configured to live on encrypted volumes that use your KMS. In Private, the disk-level encryption uses your keys. For Dedicated we can offer similar patterns with per-tenant encryption keys.
[03:16] [00:03:20] Speaker 1: sorry, quick side note — how about egress protections, we can't allow models to call out to external tools or telemetry endpoints, that's disallowed in our environment.
[03:28] Priya Shah: We have egress control policies and allowlisting. In Private you can block all outbound traffic by default. Dedicated can be locked down via network policies and VPC peering. Hosted has limited allowlist options — for bank-grade restrictions, again Private is the path we usually recommend.
[03:44] Daniel Reed: GDPR — if a European customer requests deletion, what's your SLA for deleting their data from backups and caches?
[03:52] Alex Morris: For Private we can commit to deletion SLAs in the SOW — because you control backups. For Dedicated we provide deletion tooling and confirm via logs; backups are tenant-isolated but we need to specify backup retention windows. Hosted has longer retention periods in practice, and cross-tenant backup dedupe can complicate immediate deletion.
[04:10] Sophie Tan: And what about legal process — if a regulator issues a subpoena, how do you surface audit evidence?
[04:16] Priya Shah: We can provide audit trails: who accessed what, configuration snapshots, policy changes. For Private deployments those trails reside in your logging solution. For Hosted we provide request IDs and scrubbed logs; if raw content is required we have procedures but those are gated and require lawful process and coordination.
[04:33] Maria Lopez: We need to know if any production PII or PHI will ever be used to fine-tune models in your environment — that's a non-starter unless it's strictly customer-controlled.
[04:42] Alex Morris: Redwood does not fine-tune hosted customer data into shared models. We offer isolated fine-tuning in Dedicated/Private only, with explicit consent and controls. We can do fine-tuning in a customer VPC in Private to ensure no data leaves environment.
[04:56] Daniel Reed: Can you summarize the tradeoffs again quickly? I want bullet points for execs.
[05:00] Priya Shah: Sure — Hosted: fastest to run, but limited control over raw logs and backups; better for non-sensitive workloads. Dedicated: reserved capacity, stronger tenant isolation, per-tenant keys and redaction rules — good for regulated workloads but still managed by Redwood. Private: you run control plane or we deploy in your VPC/on-prem, full control over keys, logs, and networks — highest assurance but longer onboarding and SOW.
[05:22] Jason Park: On onboarding time — what's realistic for Private?
[05:25] Liam O'Connor: Typical Private deployment for bank-sized tenant is 6–12 weeks from contract signature, depending on infra readiness and KMS/HSM provisioning, maybe faster if they have in-house automation.
[05:36] Sophie Tan: Is there any reference architecture we can share internally for legal and auditors?
[05:40] Alex Morris: Yes — we'll send a security pack and architecture diagram. Priya will provide a KMS flow and redaction matrix.
[05:48] [00:05:50] Speaker 2: A couple of specific technical asks — can Redwood suppress model outputs from being stored in observability backends for specific routes?
[05:59] Priya Shah: Yes, route-level logging controls exist. You can mark a route as sensitive and set logging to none or minimal.
[06:06] Maria Lopez: And retention windows configurable per-route?
[06:09] Priya Shah: Per-route retention is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports global retention tiers only.
[06:16] Daniel Reed: We're in financial services, so we need transaction-level trail for a subset of flows, but not full conversational logs. We might want to keep hashes and correlating IDs for audit without storing the full content. Is that feasible?
[06:28] Liam O'Connor: Totally — you can store a hash of the prompt/response plus metadata (user id, timestamp). That meets many audit requirements while protecting content.
[06:36] Sophie Tan: We'll need a reproducible mapping so we can show auditors we can link hash to the original if needed. How does that work without storing plaintext?
[06:45] Alex Morris: You can store content encrypted under your KMS and keep the decryption keys offline. The hash is a fingerprint in the audit trail; the auditor process would involve two-party verification under strict controls. We'll document the approach.
[06:58] Jason Park: What about SOC2 evidence — do you provide logs of admin actions and deployment changes?
[07:03] Priya Shah: Yes, we do. For Hosted we provide a redacted admin access log. For Dedicated/Private you can capture full admin audit logs.
[07:12] [00:07:15] Speaker 3: Sorry, slight transcription glitch — 'Redwood' sometimes shows as 'RedWood' in our notes, disregard.
[07:19] Alex Morris: No worries. Any questions on encryption at rest vs in-transit?
[07:23] Maria Lopez: We require both TLS in transit and AES-256 or better at rest, plus customer-managed keys.
[07:29] Priya Shah: Supported. We can align on AES-256 on disk and TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, plus KMS integration for keys.
[07:36] Daniel Reed: What about logs produced by model evaluation and quality metrics — those often include sample outputs, are they considered content?
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: We treat evaluation outputs as content. We recommend that evaluation runs use synthetic or anonymized datasets in Hosted; for real-data evals use Dedicated/Private with scrubbers or on-prem tooling.
[07:56] Sophie Tan: Regarding HIPAA — if we process PHI in some flows, do you sign a BAA for Private or Dedicated?
[08:02] Alex Morris: We can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted BAAs are possible in select regions/accounts but the stronger guarantee is with Private.
[08:11] Maria Lopez: Are there certifications specific to financial services you can share?
[08:15] Priya Shah: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation; for financial services we also publish penetration test summaries and can provide architecture hardening guidance. We don't have PCI attestation ourselves but our guidance aligns with PCI controls — you may need additional compensating controls.
[08:31] Daniel Reed: A few nitty-gritty questions — does Redwood ever persist raw prompts in backups or elsewhere for debugging?
[08:39] Alex Morris: By default, Hosted telemetry may store a redacted copy for debugging, but you can opt out of storing PII/PHI in logs. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and what is included in backups. We'll include explicit clauses in the SOW about not persisting raw prompts for sensitive routes.
[08:58] Jason Park: Any known limitations around on-prem GPUs and model compatibility? We want to run some quantized variants internally.
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: Our runtime supports common quantized formats; on-prem hardware compatibility depends on drivers and kernel support. We'll run a compatibility pass during onboarding.
[09:15] [00:09:20] Speaker 4: Can you describe the fallback behavior — e.g., if Private capacity is saturated, can we fall back to a hosted model while preserving residency constraints?
[09:28] Priya Shah: Fallback to Hosted would typically cross borders; we can set a policy that only allows fallback to Dedicated in same region. For absolute residency guarantees, avoid cross-hosted fallback. We can also configure a cold queue during peak to throttle rather than fail open.
[09:44] Daniel Reed: That helps. For the pilot, we want to run a subset of traffic through Private with full logging and send non-sensitive traffic to Hosted.
[09:53] Alex Morris: That is a common pattern. We'll draft a pilot SOW that lays out routes, data categories, retention, and KPIs.
[09:59] Sophie Tan: Please include acceptance criteria around deletion — auditors want evidence in a 30/60 day window.
[10:05] Alex Morris: We'll include deletion acceptance tests and verification steps in the SOW.
[10:10] Maria Lopez: Two follow-ups — can Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM for RBAC?
[10:15] Priya Shah: Yes, SAML and SCIM are supported across Dedicated and Hosted control planes; for Private you can integrate with your IdP directly.
[10:23] Jason Park: Any sample helm or terraform repos for Private deployment?
[10:27] Liam O'Connor: We'll share an infra repo skeleton and an ops checklist.
[10:30] [00:10:32] Speaker 5: There's a question about change control — how are runtime updates handled in Dedicated/Private?
[10:36] Priya Shah: For Dedicated, updates are scheduled with maintenance windows and we do canary rollouts per-reservation. For Private, customers control update cadence; Redwood provides patches and tooling but you can defer non-critical updates.
[10:49] Daniel Reed: Any SLA numbers you can share for latency and uptime for Dedicated?
[10:54] Alex Morris: We have SLA tiers in Dedicated: 99.9% or higher depending on reserved commitment; latency SLOs depend on instance size and model family — we'll share typical 95th percentile numbers for budgets you care about.
[11:08] Sophie Tan: For audits, we'd like access to redacted incident postmortems if an outage affects our tenant. Is that available?
[11:15] Priya Shah: Yes, we provide postmortems and RCA summaries to customers. For Dedicated and Private we can share more granular internal timelines.
[11:25] Maria Lopez: One last technical — can we disable telemetry pings to third-party analytics providers?
[11:31] Alex Morris: Yes, that's controllable at deploy time for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has minimal internal telemetry which we can restrict for enterprise tiers.
[11:39] Daniel Reed: Great. I think we covered most of it. Let's recap next steps.
[11:43] Alex Morris: Recap: Redwood sends security pack (SOC2, ISO), architecture diagram, KMS flow, sample SOW for a Private pilot. Aurora to provide sample dataset and list of sensitive routes. Schedule SE deep dive week of 3/24.
[11:57] Sophie Tan: I'll expect the pack and we'll coordinate with our audit team.
[12:01] Alex Morris: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

Meeting end.
